_comment: Shared schema contract for the SQLite database, generated from the Android
Android asserts that its exported schema still matches this file; iOS asserts
that the database GRDB creates matches it, by introspecting PRAGMA table_info,
index_list and foreign_key_list. Neither platform can drift.
Room's own bookkeeping (room_master_table, user_version) is NOT part of the
contract: a database FILE is not an interchange format between the platforms.
The JSON backup is. What is shared is the table shape, so the domain logic and
the queries mean the same thing on both sides.
Column order follows the Room export and is significant only for readability.

entries.utcOffsetSeconds is NOT NULL from schema 4 on: MIGRATION_3_4 backfilled every row that predated the column with the offset the device zone had at that row's instant, then rebuilt the table with the constraint, because SQLite cannot add one to an existing column. The rebuild also removed the reason the column sits last, which was that ALTER TABLE appends; the order is kept because moving it would churn this contract for nothing.

logical_day_key holds one row and records which day-change time entries.logicalDate was last derived under. Both columns are nullable and mean, together, "not derived yet"; that is the state a finished migration and a finished backup import leave behind. While the key is set, every row satisfies logicalDate == DayResolver.resolve(timestampMillis, utcOffsetSeconds, changeHour, changeMinute).
